extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (PhD students, postdocs, permanent researchers, senior research staff) looking for FNRS calls and funding opportunities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metadata for FNRS funding calls: eligibility profiles, call categories, timelines, thematic scopes and activity types used to determine who may apply and what is funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant profile (PhD (R1), Postdoc (R2), Permanent research status (R3), Senior research position (R4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile: PhD (R1), Postdoc (R2), Permanent research status (R3), Senior research position (R4). Calls indicate which researcher profiles are eligible to apply (examples across calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each call lists the accepted applicant profiles. Examples from the page: M-ERA.NET Call 2026 — Permanent research status (R3) and Senior research position (R4); Tournesol PHC — Postdoc (R2), Permanent research status (R3) and Senior research position (R4); Scientific meeting abroad (OUT) and Stay Abroad/Summer Workshops or Courses (OUT) — PhD (R1), Postdoc (R2), Permanent research status (R3), Senior research position (R4). Applicants must check the call's 'Profile' field to confirm eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call category / funding instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Category labels used to classify calls (examples on the page): International & Mobility; Dissemination & Exchange; Projects, credits, ...; Research Mandates, Fellowships, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Category' indicates the type/aim of the funding (e.g., mobility support, dissemination, project grants, fellowships). Applicants should choose calls whose category matches the proposed activity. Examples: 'International projects' shown as Category 'International & Mobility'; 'Organization of a scientific meeting' shown as Category 'Dissemination & Exchange'; 'Infrastructures & Large Equipments 2024' shown as Category 'Projects, credits, ...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening and closing dates (application timeline and deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each call displays explicit opening and closing timestamps (e.g., Opening 04 March 2026 14:00 — Closing 19 May 2026 14:00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted within the posted opening/closing window. Check exact dates/times for each call; missing the deadline closes eligibility. Example items on the page show precise opening/closing datetimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodicity / recurrence of the call
rubrics_metrics.description: Some calls include a 'Periodicity' field indicating recurrence (example: 'Annual').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a call is periodic (e.g., annual), applicants may plan to apply in future cycles when ineligible in the current one. Verify periodicity to schedule proposals and institutional approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic eligibility / eligible topics (example: AstraZeneca Foundation Scientific Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some competitions specify thematic topics that proposals must address. Example given for the AstraZeneca Foundation Scientific Awards: Eligible topics are 'Cancer as a Systemic Disease: Insights on Organ Crosstalk'; 'Zoonoses and Climate Change as Emerging Threats to Human Health'; 'Multi-Omics for Routine Risk Stratification and Prevention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must align with the explicitly listed topics for topic-specific awards. Applicants should ensure their project clearly addresses one of the eligible themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain / research area tags (SVS, SEN, SHS, Sustainability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls include domain tags indicating the scientific domain(s) targeted (examples on the page: SVS, SEN, SHS, Sustainability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check these tags to confirm disciplinary fit. Calls may restrict eligibility or prioritization to particular domains (e.g., SVS/SEN/SHS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity types eligible for funding (mobility, meetings, stays, contact groups, doctoral schools)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists funded activity types such as 'Scientific meeting abroad (OUT)', 'Organization of a scientific meeting', 'Stay Abroad/Summer Workshops or Courses (OUT)', 'Contact Groups', 'Doctoral schools', 'Scientific Stay Scholarship (IN and OUT)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each call or instrument specifies which activity types are supported; applicants must select the appropriate instrument that matches the intended activity (travel/stay/meeting/course/doctoral school).

rubrics_metrics.name: International / bilateral call formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Some calls are international or bilateral in nature (examples: 'NSFC (China) - Bilateral Call (2026)', 'M-ERA.NET Call 2026', 'Tournesol PHC', 'Opening of the 2026 bilateral call with the NSFC (China)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bilateral/international calls typically require or encourage international partners and compliance with partner-country rules. Applicants should verify partner-institution eligibility and any joint-application procedures specific to bilateral calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding instrument labels and scope examples (Grants & Fellowships, Infrastructures & Large Equipments, FRArt)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site distinguishes instruments by label and scope, e.g., 'Grants & Fellowships 2025' (Research Mandates, Fellowships...), 'Infrastructures & Large Equipments 2024' (Projects, credits,...), 'FRArt 2025' (Art Research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels signal the intended use of funds and target applicants; choose the instrument aligned with project type (personnel fellowships vs. equipment vs. art research). Read the instrument page for specific eligibility and allowed costs.
